title: Quiz yourself for 10 minutes
reason: Testing yourself helps you remember more than just rereading notes.

title: Do a practice test
reason: Practice tests are one of the best-proven ways to get ready for an exam.

title: Spread study over three days
reason: Short study sessions spread over several days stick better than one big cram.

title: Make flashcards for one topic
reason: Flashcards turn studying into self-testing, which builds memory.

title: Quiz yourself on today's class
reason: A quick quiz on the same day helps new lessons stick.

title: Explain a topic out loud
reason: Explaining ideas in your own words helps you understand them.

title: Mix up practice problems
reason: Mixing different problem types helps you learn when to use each method.

title: Ask why for each fact
reason: Asking yourself why a fact is true makes it easier to remember.

title: Plan when you'll study
reason: Deciding exactly when and where you'll study makes you more likely to do it.

title: Start homework right after snack
reason: Linking homework to the same daily cue helps it become a habit.

title: Revisit last week's notes
reason: Coming back to older material later is a proven way to remember it longer.

title: Pack your school bag tonight
reason: Getting ready the night before makes busy mornings calmer.

title: Phone away while studying
reason: Keeping distractions out of reach makes it easier to stay focused.

title: Study with a classmate
reason: Testing each other gives you practice and keeps studying social.

title: Pick a set bedtime
reason: Going to bed at the same time each night helps your body clock.

title: Same wake-up time daily
reason: Waking at the same time, even on weekends, builds healthy sleep.

title: Screens off before bed
reason: Turning devices off 30 minutes before bed can help you fall asleep.

title: Phone out of bedroom tonight
reason: Tech use near bedtime is linked with poorer sleep, so give it a break.

title: Make a bedtime routine
reason: A calm, relaxing routine tells your body it's time to sleep.

title: Keep your room cool, quiet
reason: A quiet, cool, relaxing room is easier to sleep in.

title: Dim lights after dinner
reason: Less bright light in the evening helps you get sleepy.

title: No caffeine after lunch
reason: Caffeine later in the day can make it harder to sleep.

title: Plan enough sleep tonight
reason: Kids 6–12 need 9–12 hours, teens 8–10, and adults 7 or more.

title: Set a bedtime reminder
reason: A reminder helps you start winding down on time.

title: Keep a sleep diary
reason: Writing down bed and wake times helps you spot sleep patterns.

title: Light snack, not big meal
reason: Big meals right before bed can make sleep harder.

title: Use bed just for sleep
reason: Keeping homework and games out of bed helps your brain link bed with sleep.

title: Get up if can't sleep
reason: If you're awake 20 minutes, a quiet, screen-free activity can help.

title: Write tomorrow's top three
reason: Choosing what matters most helps you decide what can wait.

title: Make one if-then plan
reason: Plans like 'If it's 4pm, then I start my essay' make goals much more likely to happen.

title: Break a big task down
reason: Small, manageable steps feel easier to start and finish.

title: Plan your week ahead
reason: Deciding when and where you'll do things helps you follow through.

title: Link a habit to routine
reason: Doing a new habit right after something you already do helps it stick.

title: Note three wins today
reason: Noticing what you got done builds confidence and lowers stress.

title: Say no to one extra
reason: Turning down a task when you're overloaded protects your time and energy.

title: Reward a small step
reason: Giving yourself a small, healthy treat for progress keeps you going.

title: Phone in another room
reason: Keeping temptations out of reach makes focusing easier.

title: Start with just 5 minutes
reason: Tiny starts are easier, and small wins build confidence for bigger ones.

title: Do the hardest task first
reason: Planning when you'll tackle the toughest task helps you actually start it.

title: Ask for help today
reason: Getting help or sharing the load is a proven way to lower stress.

title: Track one habit daily
reason: A simple tick sheet helps you see a new habit getting easier.

title: Track spending for a week
reason: Seeing where your money goes is the first step to a budget.

title: Ask: need or want?
reason: Covering needs before wants is a wise money habit.

title: Set a savings goal
reason: Knowing exactly what you're saving for makes saving easier.

title: Make a simple budget
reason: A budget shows money coming in, going out, and what you can save.

title: Save 10% of your pay
reason: Saving at least 10 percent of what you earn builds a safety cushion.

title: Start an emergency fund
reason: Money set aside for surprises helps you avoid costly borrowing.

title: Put coins in a jar
reason: A savings jar makes progress toward your goal easy to see.

title: Learn about compound interest
reason: Saving early lets your money grow on its own interest over time.

title: Compare banks or credit unions
reason: Comparing places to keep money safe helps you pick what fits you.

title: Talk money with family
reason: Money conversations at home help build good money skills early.

title: Sort bills: fixed or changing
reason: Knowing which costs stay the same each month makes budgeting simpler.

title: Compare before you buy
reason: Comparing options helps you pick what meets your needs and budget.

title: Review this week's spending
reason: A weekly check helps you see if you're on track for your goal.

title: Brush teeth two minutes
reason: Brushing twice a day for about 2 minutes keeps your mouth healthy.

title: Brush right before bed
reason: Night-time brushing is especially important for your teeth.

title: Floss before brushing
reason: Flossing removes plaque along the gum line that brushing can miss.

title: Carry a water bottle
reason: Drinking regularly through the day keeps you hydrated.

title: Swap soda for water
reason: Water is a healthy choice, and sugary drinks can harm your teeth.

title: Add fruit to breakfast
reason: Fruit gives you vitamins and fibre, and every portion counts.

title: Add a veggie to dinner
reason: Eating a variety of fruit and veg helps keep you healthy.

title: Eat a rainbow today
reason: Different colours of fruit and veg give different nutrients.

title: Wash hands before eating
reason: Handwashing with soap is one of the best ways to stay healthy.

title: Scrub hands for 20 seconds
reason: Humming Happy Birthday twice is a fun 20-second timer.

title: Eat regular meals today
reason: Regular, balanced meals help your energy and focus.

title: Pack a fruit snack
reason: Having fruit with you makes the healthy choice the easy one.

title: Refill water after sport
reason: Extra fluids help replace what you lose when you sweat.

title: Take a 10-minute walk
reason: Short bits of activity add up and are better than none.

title: Brisk 30-minute walk
reason: A brisk walk can lift your mood and lower stress.

title: Be active 60 minutes
reason: Kids and teens 6–17 need 60 minutes of activity every day.

title: Jump or skip 5 minutes
reason: Jumping and running help build strong bones.

title: Do push-ups or climbing
reason: Muscle-strengthening activities are recommended at least 3 days a week for kids.

title: Strength moves twice weekly
reason: Adults need muscle-strengthening activity at least 2 days a week.

title: Dance to three songs
reason: Moving to music counts as activity and can boost your mood.

title: Play an active game
reason: Games like tag get your heart beating faster and are fun.

title: Stand up and move hourly
reason: Sitting less and moving more brings health benefits.

title: Walk or bike somewhere
reason: Walking to school or nearby places counts as moderate activity (when safe).

title: Try a new sport
reason: Finding an activity you enjoy makes it easier to keep moving.

title: Stretch for 5 minutes
reason: Stretching helps release the muscle tension that stress causes.

title: Run, bike or swim hard
reason: Vigorous activity at least 3 days a week helps kids and teens get fitter.

title: Eat dinner with family
reason: A regular family meal time builds belonging and support.

title: Message a friend you miss
reason: Reaching out keeps friendships strong and fights loneliness.

title: Plan a day with friends
reason: Spending time with friends you haven't seen in a while lifts wellbeing.

title: Thank someone today
reason: Saying thank you is a simple act of kindness that feels good.

title: Ask someone how they are
reason: Really listening to the answer helps you connect.

title: Help someone with something
reason: Giving help creates good feelings and a sense of purpose.

title: Screen-free family game night
reason: Switching off the TV to play together builds closer bonds.

title: Video call far-away family
reason: Video chats help you stay close when you live apart.

title: Sit with someone new
reason: Having lunch with a classmate or colleague builds connection.

title: Visit someone who's lonely
reason: Spending time with someone who needs company helps you both.

title: Volunteer for one hour
reason: Volunteering in your community can boost wellbeing and connection.

title: Talk, don't just text
reason: Real conversations build relationships better than messages alone.

title: Share good news with someone
reason: Sharing positive moments is one way relationships boost wellbeing.

title: Write three good things
reason: Being specific about what you're grateful for supports mental health.

title: Breathe slowly for 3 minutes
reason: Slow belly breathing can calm your body and mind.

title: Try 5 minutes of mindfulness
reason: Short mindfulness practice can lower stress and worry.

title: Name how you feel
reason: Silently naming a feeling, like 'this is worry', helps you step back from it.

title: Notice five things around you
reason: Paying attention to the present moment can improve wellbeing.

title: Reframe one worry
reason: Looking at a problem a new way can lower stress.

title: Be kind to yourself today
reason: Noting what you did, not what you missed, builds self-compassion.

title: Spend time in nature
reason: Time in green spaces, even a park, can improve your mood.

title: Talk to someone you trust
reason: Sharing how you feel with a trusted person is a healthy way to cope.

title: Mindful walk to class
reason: A regular walk is a great time to notice the world around you.

title: Limit comparison scrolling
reason: Comparing looks on social media is linked to feeling worse about yourself.

title: Follow accounts that support you
reason: Using social media for support and connection can be good for you.

title: Do one thing you enjoy
reason: Doing something you enjoy every day helps refill your energy.

title: Learn a new recipe
reason: Learning a new skill like cooking boosts confidence.

title: Practise an instrument 15 minutes
reason: Short, regular practice spread over days helps skills stick.

title: Learn ten new words
reason: Learning a language is a great way to build a sense of purpose.

title: Fix or build something
reason: A small DIY project, like fixing a bike, is a satisfying new skill.

title: Watch a how-to video
reason: Free tutorials make it easy to start learning something new.

title: Start a creative hobby
reason: Hobbies like painting or writing can lift your mood and confidence.

title: Read for 20 minutes
reason: Reading for fun is a pleasurable way to keep learning.

title: Quiz yourself on a hobby
reason: Testing yourself works for any skill, not just school subjects.

title: Join a club or class
reason: Classes outside school build skills and new friendships.

title: Teach someone a skill
reason: Explaining something to others deepens your own understanding.

title: Write a short story
reason: Writing is a challenging hobby that builds creativity.

title: Take on a new responsibility
reason: Trying a new role at school or work builds skills and purpose.

title: Practise one skill daily
reason: Practising the same skill at the same time each day helps it become a habit.

title: Take a 15-minute break
reason: Even when you're busy, keeping fun activities helps you handle stress.

title: Listen to favourite music
reason: Singing along to songs you love is a simple way to unwind.

title: Watch something funny
reason: Laughter and humour can benefit your mental and physical health.

title: Have a warm bath

title: Relax muscles head to toe
reason: Tensing then relaxing each muscle group can reduce anxiety.

title: Read just for fun
reason: Reading something you enjoy is a healthy way to recharge.

title: Do a low-stress hobby
reason: Low-stress hobbies like drawing or crafts help you unwind.

title: Sit outside for 10 minutes
reason: Noticing nature, even a city park, can calm your mind.

title: Try gentle yoga
reason: Yoga and stretching can ease stress and help a busy mind.

title: Plan a rest evening
reason: Scheduling regular relaxing time is part of good self-care.

title: Screen-free wind-down time
reason: Putting down screens helps calm your mind before bed.

title: Have fun with friends
reason: Fun with friends is a proven stress reliever.

title: Make art for fun
reason: Making art just for enjoyment can help relieve stress.
